## Report on `region.fasta` (`>locus_007`)

**Sequence:** one 3,000 bp linear DNA molecule. Composition: A 682, C 787, G 864, T 667 → **GC = 55.0 %**, with a mild G-over-C skew (G−C)/(G+C) ≈ +0.047. Nothing suggests contamination or low quality.

### Notable feature: a tandem repeat array (minisatellite)

The one striking thing in this sequence is a **tandemly repeated 33 bp unit** in the middle of the molecule. A 12-mer self-comparison of the whole 3 kb finds repeat diagonals **only** at offsets 33, 66, 99, 132, 165, 198, 231 and 264 bp (i.e. exact multiples of the 33 bp period), all confined to coordinates ~1,847–2,134. No other repeated sequence exists anywhere else in the 3 kb.

| Feature | Coordinates (1-based, + strand) |
|---|---|
| Tandem array (full extent) | **~1826 – 2122** |
| 8 near-identical 33 bp copies | **1859 – 2122** (264 bp) |
| Degenerate 9th (5′-most) copy | **1826 – 1858** |
| Consensus unit | `CTCATGTCCTGAGGGCCATTGAGCGTACATCAT` |

Copy-to-consensus identity is 30–32 of 33 bp for all eight full copies, so the array is very homogeneous (a classic minisatellite). The 5′-most copy (1826–1858) is divergent and retains only the 3′ 11 bp (`GCGTACATCAT`) of the consensus; the array boundary on the 3′ side is sharp, with unrelated sequence resuming after 2122.

**Consequence for reading frames:** 33 is divisible by 3, so the repeat does not disrupt frame. As expected, conceptual translation of the array gives repetitive peptides on both strands — e.g. an ATG-initiated plus-strand ORF at **1831–2238** (408 nt) yielding `MRRGAMRTSCHVLRAIERTSSHVLRAIERTS…`, and a minus-strand ORF ending at plus-coordinate 2122 whose 11-aa blocks (`MYAQWPSGHE`, `MYAQWPAGHE`, …) correspond one-to-one to the 33 bp units. These are translation artefacts of the repeat rather than evidence of a conserved protein; I found no non-repetitive, obviously protein-coding segment.

### Minor observations
- A second, non-repetitive plus-strand ORF runs 731–1066 (336 nt, 112 aa) in frame 1; it has no repeats and no obvious character.
- Short homopolymer runs only, all unremarkable: `G6` 25–30, `A5` 122–126, `G5` 147–151, `G5` 216–220, `C5` 693–697, `C5` 1287–1291, `G5` 2256–2260, `C6` 2494–2499, `A6` 2742–2747, `G5` 2896–2900, `A8` 2955–2962.
- No inverted repeats/hairpins (stem ≥ 8 bp) and no short-period (2–6 bp) microsatellites were detected.

### Summary
Apart from a slightly elevated GC content, the only notable sequence feature is a **homogeneous 33 bp tandem repeat array spanning approximately nt 1826–2122, comprising eight full copies (1859–2122) plus one degenerate 5′ copy (1826–1858)**. Because the unit length is a multiple of three, the array lies in-frame with flanking ORFs and produces strongly repetitive predicted peptides on both strands. Beyond this minisatellite, the region shows no other structural or compositional anomalies. (Caveat: this is a purely computational characterisation; no database similarity search was performed, so biological function cannot be assigned.)
